note: Recorded by hand from https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_integrate_services_list.html before the parser was written. The page is one table of 52 rows. Column 3 (Supports trusted access) and column 4 (Supports delegated administrator) are two different capabilities, so they are two features, not one. Counted by hand from the table: trusted access is Yes on 51 of 52 rows, No only on Amazon EventBridge; delegated administrator is Yes on 40 rows and No on 12 (AWS Artifact, AWS Billing and Cost Management, AWS Control Tower, AWS Directory Service, Amazon EventBridge, Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud, AWS Marketplace, Amazon Q Developer, AWS Resource Access Manager, Service Quotas, Tag policies, AWS Well-Architected Tool). 14 of the 52 row labels are product or feature names that resolveService does not match, so they are unresolved and never counted: AWS Account Management, AWS Agent Registry, AWS Billing and Cost Management, AWS CloudFormation Stacksets, AWS Cost Optimization Hub, EC2 Capacity Manager, Amazon Inspector (ambiguous across inspector, inspector2 and inspector-scan), AWS Managed Services (AMS) Self-Service Reporting (SSR), AWS Marketplace Private Marketplace, AWS Marketplace procurement insights dashboard, Amazon S3 Storage Lens, Tag policies, Amazon VPC IP Address Manager (IPAM), Amazon VPC Reachability Analyzer. That leaves 38 resolved rows, so trusted access counts 37 covered and 1 excluded, and delegated administrator counts 28 covered and 10 excluded. No two resolved rows share a service id.
